title: w-conversations: executing the conversations v1 plan

content: Before any work: reply with your pij id, spawnId, model+effort, cwd, and the word CANARY-OK. Do not start work yet.
CANARY-OK. pij id pij-armed-ape, spawnId s1787822150755-26769, model github-copilot/claude-opus-5 effort high. Holding before cutting a worktree until the go arrives.

Canary verified. GO on orientation: read in the briefs authority order, then cut the worktree and ack with your numbered per-phase plan of attack BEFORE any code. Plan corrections with file:line evidence outrank the plan.

Two evidence-backed plan corrections before coding. A3: the --repo and --path filters would silently return ZERO conversation hits, because the search CTE reaches a repository through elements to worktree_files to worktrees to repos, and a turn element has no worktree_files row at all, yet workshop 005 promises anchor filters compose. A4: turn elements need a reserved parser_version, because get_elements hard-fails on a blob_sha and parser_version pair without exactly one file root, so a canonical form hashing equal to a source blob would corrupt that file's next scan.

A3 APPROVED and thank you for raising it at phase 1 where it belongs. A4 APPROVED: reserved parser_version conversation/1 -- the blob-collision hard-fail is exactly the class of trap this fleet's ack cycle exists to catch pre-code. Phase 1: code.

STOP-AND-ASK on the anchor column. Measured: roots.rs:173 deletes the repos row inside the removal transaction, so workshop 005's repo_id foreign key cannot hold -- once ANY conversation is anchored to a repo, removing its last worktree raises foreign_key_violation and the whole remove fails. That breaks ac-0007. Recommend storing the anchor as TEXT repo_identity with no foreign key: exact pointer semantics, survives removal, and re-links automatically when the repo is added back because repos.identity is UNIQUE.

RULED: TEXT repo_identity, no FK. Your argument is complete: it is the codebase's own value-pointer doctrine, it survives removal, auto-relinks through repos.identity UNIQUE, and answers for never-registered anchors. Record the no-FK-integrity cost in the migration comment the way 0004 records D7. The workshop DDL sketch is hereby amended by your evidence.

STOP-AND-ASK, production defect found by a phase-2 test. GC silently deletes pending embed jobs for live content. The level-0 predicate tests a job by payload raw_hash. A summarize job has that field; an EMBED job does not, because it carries a batch as items -- so the predicate reads NULL, concludes nothing references it, and deletes it. The elements stay, the summaries stay, status reports an empty queue, and the content is simply absent from every semantic search. Reproduced on the pure code path with no conversations, and confirmed pre-existing by re-running against main's exact predicate.

RULED: fix it in your phase-2 PR. Requirements: the fix rides as its own fix-prefixed commit; the predicate covers both spaces as you measured; and RECOVERY, because the damage is already done -- Jordan restarted his daemon mid-scan twice today with thousands pending and GC runs at every boot, so his live index likely has elements whose vectors were silently reaped.

Fix landed with recovery. The predicate now asks both vector spaces, because the item hashes live in two: a raw batch's hashes are element raw_hashes, and a smart batch's are smart_content text_hashes which reach an element only through the summary row. A raw-only fix would still have reaped every summary vector waiting to be bought. missing_embeddings derives the backlog from the SCHEMA rather than the queue, which is the only shape that can work when the evidence destroyed was the queue rows themselves.
Fourth commit accepted. Then GO PHASE 3 -- remember the conv: arm replaces the NOT-IMPLEMENTED return and keeps the guid and turn parse in fs3_core::address.

Phase 3 surface built. The critic-finding-4 trap is real and mutation-checked: a turn quoting a line of code shares one raw hash with it, the resolver takes the lowest-id element, and without the kind predicate bound in the resolution join as well as the candidate CTE the conversation search resolves to the CODE element and prints an el: address for a turn. Removing that one predicate turns the assertion from turn to function.
Phase 3 on. Report when the dogfood proof is in.

Running it now against a private dogfood database with the real Azure providers, so the search proof is a real embedding rather than a fake one. Importing this very session as the transcript: the fleet conversation that built conversations is the honest thing to index first.
Exit proof captured: imported, grown, searched by meaning, windowed around the hit, and outlined. The conversation that built conversations is now findable by asking for it.
